vegan.title: Vegan Adas Polo
vegan.description: The same saffron lentil rice with caramelized onions, dates and raisins, made with olive oil instead of butter. Serve it with dairy-free yogurt or a Shirazi salad.

ingredients.item: saffron threads, ground with a pinch of sugar
salt, for the rice water, plus more to taste
dairy-free yogurt or Shirazi salad, to serve

steps: Rinse the rice in cool water until it runs almost clear, then soak it in salted water for at least 30 minutes. Bloom the saffron in the hot water.
Simmer the lentils in plenty of water for 15 to 20 minutes, until just tender but still holding their shape. Drain and season with a pinch of salt.

Cook the onions in the oil over medium heat for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden and sweet. Stir in the cinnamon and turmeric for 30 seconds, then lift out half the onions for the top.
Add 2 tbsp olive oil, the raisins and dates to the onions left in the pan and warm for 2 minutes, just until the raisins plump. Set aside.

Bring a large pot of water and 2 tbsp salt to a rolling boil. Drain the rice, add it and boil 5 to 6 minutes, until the grains are soft outside but still have a firm bite in the center. Drain and gently fold in the lentils.
Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a heavy nonstick pot with 2 tbsp water and 1 tbsp of the saffron water. Spread a thin layer of rice over the bottom and press it down: this becomes the tahdig.
Pile the rest of the rice in a loose mound. Poke 4 or 5 holes down to the bottom with a spoon handle, drizzle with the remaining olive oil and drizzle with the rest of the saffron water.

Wrap the lid in a clean kitchen towel, cover tightly and cook 10 minutes on medium until you hear sizzling, then 40 to 45 minutes on low. Spoon onto a platter, scatter the fruit and onions over, and serve the crust broken into pieces.
vegan.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Parboiling then steaming is the Persian method that keeps every grain separate and long. Stop boiling the moment the outside is soft and the center still resists.
The towel under the lid catches steam that would otherwise drip back and make the rice soggy.
Listen for the sizzle before turning the heat down: it means the bottom is starting to crisp into tahdig.
vegan.make_ahead: Cook the lentils and onions up to 2 days ahead. Leftover rice keeps 4 days; reheat with a splash of water, covered, so it steams.

vegetarian.title: Vegetarian Ajiaco
vegetarian.description: All the corn, three potatoes and guascas of the classic, with white beans in place of the chicken and a vegetable broth base.

ingredients.item: russet potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced
papas criollas or baby yellow potatoes
white beans or hearts of palm, drained
Mexican crema or heavy cream, to serve

steps: Simmer the broth with the green onions, garlic, cilantro, salt and pepper for 15 minutes, then discard the green onions and cilantro.
Add the corn, russet potatoes and red potatoes. Simmer 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until the russets start to fall apart and thicken the soup.
Add the papas criollas and guascas and simmer 15 to 20 minutes more, until the small potatoes are tender and the broth is creamy.
Stir in the beans or sliced hearts of palm for the last 5 minutes and taste for salt.
Ladle into deep bowls with a piece of corn in each and serve the cream, capers and avocado on the side.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: The three potatoes each do a job: russets dissolve to thicken, red potatoes hold their shape, and the little yellow ones add buttery flavor.
Guascas gives ajiaco its signature taste. Look for it dried in Latin markets; dried oregano is a distant but workable stand-in.
Keep the soup at a gentle simmer so the beans stay whole while the russets melt.
vegetarian.make_ahead: Keeps 3 days in the fridge and thickens as it sits; thin it with water when reheating. Add the cream, capers and avocado only when serving.

vegetarian.title: Vegetarian Amok
vegetarian.description: The same fragrant coconut custard with tofu and mushrooms in place of fish, and soy sauce and miso instead of fish sauce and shrimp paste.

ingredients.item: extra-firm tofu and oyster mushrooms, cut into bite-size pieces
lemongrass, tender parts only, thinly sliced
galangal or ginger, peeled and sliced
makrut lime leaves, stems removed (2 for garnish)
dried red chilies, soaked in hot water
coconut milk, plus 1/4 cup thick coconut cream for topping
red chili, cut in thin strips, to garnish

steps: Make the kroeung paste: pound or blend the lemongrass, galangal, turmeric, 2 lime leaves, shallots, garlic, drained chilies and white miso with a splash of water until smooth.
Whisk the paste with the coconut milk, egg, light soy sauce and sugar. Fold in the tofu and mushrooms and let them sit 10 minutes.
Soften the banana leaves over a flame or in hot water and fold them into four cups, pinning the corners with toothpicks. Line each cup (or ramekin) with shredded spinach.
Spoon the tofu and curry into the cups. Steam over simmering water, covered, for 20 to 25 minutes, until the custard is set but still trembles slightly.
Top each with a spoon of coconut cream, finely shredded lime leaf and chili strips. Serve hot with rice.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: The egg is what turns the curry into amok's soft, mousse-like custard. Steam gently: a hard boil makes it grainy.
Fresh kroeung is the soul of the dish. Make a double batch and freeze half for next time.
Press the tofu for 15 minutes so it soaks up the curry instead of watering it down.
vegetarian.make_ahead: The kroeung paste keeps 1 week in the fridge or 3 months frozen. Amok is best eaten freshly steamed.

vegetarian.title: Vegetarian Tomato Bredie
vegetarian.description: The same warmly spiced, jammy tomato stew made with chickpeas, butternut squash and potatoes.

ingredients.item: chili flakes or 1 fresh green chili, chopped
ripe tomatoes, chopped, or 2 cans (14 oz) chopped tomatoes
steamed rice and chopped parsley, to serve

steps: Cook the onions in the oil in a heavy pot over medium heat for 10 minutes until soft and golden. Add the garlic, ginger, cinnamon, cloves, cardamom, bay leaves and chili and stir for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, tomato paste, sugar and broth. Simmer, covered, for 20 minutes to build the sauce.
Add the potatoes and squash and simmer, covered, for 25 minutes. Stir in the chickpeas and cook 10 minutes more, until the vegetables are tender.
Uncover for the last few minutes if the sauce is thin. Taste for salt and sugar and serve over rice with parsley.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Simmering the sauce on its own first gives the spices time to soften into the tomatoes, the way the lamb's long braise would.
vegetarian.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen.

vegetarian.title: Vegetarian Chakhchoukha
vegetarian.description: Torn semolina bread soaked in a spiced tomato broth with extra chickpeas, potatoes and vegetables.

ingredients.item: potatoes, peeled and cut in chunks
chickpeas, drained, or 1 cup dried, soaked overnight
rougag or thin semolina flatbread (or thin pita), torn into small pieces

steps: Heat the oil in a large pot. Add the onion and garlic and cook 5 minutes, then stir in the tomato paste, tomatoes, ras el hanout, paprika, cayenne, pepper and salt for 2 minutes.
Add the water (and dried chickpeas if using). Bring to a boil, add the potatoes, then simmer, covered, for 15 minutes (45 if using dried chickpeas).
Add the carrots (and canned chickpeas) and simmer 15 minutes, then the zucchini for 10 minutes more, until the vegetables are tender and the sauce is rich and slightly reduced.
Meanwhile, steam the torn bread over the stew or in a steamer basket for 10 minutes, tossing once, until soft and pliable. Toss with the butter.
Pile the bread in a wide dish and ladle over plenty of the hot sauce, letting it soak in. Top with the chickpeas and vegetables and serve extra sauce on the side.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Steaming the bread first makes it soft enough to drink up the sauce without turning to mush.
The sauce should be plentiful and thin enough to soak in, more like a broth than a thick stew.
vegetarian.make_ahead: The marqa stew keeps 3 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen. Steam and soak the bread just before serving.

vegetarian.title: Vegetarian Encebollado
vegetarian.description: The same cumin-tomato broth and tender yuca, with meaty hearts of palm and oyster mushrooms in place of the tuna.

ingredients.item: hearts of palm (2 cans) and oyster mushrooms, torn
yuca (cassava), fresh or frozen, peeled and cut in chunks
limes, juiced, plus wedges to serve
plantain chips (chifles), popcorn and hot sauce, to serve

steps: Make the curtido: soak the red onions in salted warm water for 5 minutes, drain, then toss with the diced tomatoes, lime juice, a pinch of salt and some cilantro. Let it sit while you cook.
Make a refrito: cook the white onion in the oil for 5 minutes, then add the chopped tomatoes, garlic, cumin and chili powder and cook 5 minutes more, until thick.
Add the water, salt and cilantro stems and bring to a boil. Add the mushrooms and simmer 5 minutes, then lift them out.
Add the yuca to the broth and simmer 25 to 30 minutes, until very tender. Remove the woody center strand from each piece, and mash a few pieces against the pot to thicken the broth.
Return the mushrooms, add the sliced hearts of palm, warm through and taste for salt. Serve in deep bowls, heaped with curtido, with chifles, lime wedges and hot sauce on the side.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Hearts of palm flake like fish and add the gentle sea-like flavor; add them at the end so they stay tender.
Frozen yuca is already peeled and cooks more evenly than fresh, and it works perfectly here.
The curtido is half the dish: the sharp, crunchy onions cut the rich broth.
vegetarian.make_ahead: The broth and yuca keep 3 days in the fridge; add the mushrooms and hearts of palm when reheating. The curtido keeps 3 days.

vegetarian.title: Vegetarian Griot
vegetarian.description: Big oyster mushrooms and tofu soaked in the same sour orange and epis marinade, then fried until crisp, with pikliz and plantains.

ingredients.item: oyster or king oyster mushrooms, torn into large pieces
extra-firm tofu, pressed and cut in 1 1/2-inch cubes
sour orange juice, or half orange and half lime juice
epis (blend of parsley, green onion, peppers, garlic, thyme and oil)
pikliz, fried plantains and rice, to serve

steps: Toss the mushrooms and tofu with the sour orange juice, epis, garlic, chili, thyme, salt and pepper. Marinate 30 minutes to 2 hours.
Lift the pieces from the marinade, pat them dry and toss with the cornstarch.
Heat 1 inch of oil to 350°F and fry in batches for 4 to 5 minutes, until deep golden and crisp.
Drain and serve hot with pikliz, plantains and rice, with a squeeze of sour orange on top.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: A light coat of cornstarch gives the crackly crust that braised pork gets naturally.
vegetarian.make_ahead: Marinate up to a day ahead; fry just before serving.

vegetarian.title: Vegetarian Larb
vegetarian.description: Crumbled tofu and mushrooms dressed with lime, soy sauce and chili, with fresh herbs and toasted rice powder.

ingredients.item: extra-firm tofu and mushrooms, finely chopped (about 1 lb total)
uncooked sticky or jasmine rice, for toasted rice powder
sticky rice, lettuce cups, cucumber and long beans, to serve

steps: Toast the rice in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring constantly, for 10 to 15 minutes, until deep golden and smelling like popcorn. Cool and grind to a coarse powder.
Cook the tofu and mushrooms in a lightly oiled pan over medium-high heat for 6 to 8 minutes, until the mushrooms have released their liquid and the tofu is lightly golden.
Take the pan off the heat. Stir in the soy sauce, lime juice, sugar and chili flakes. Taste: it should be sour, salty and spicy all at once.
Add the shallots, green onions, most of the herbs and 2 tbsp of the toasted rice powder and toss.
Pile onto a plate, sprinkle with the rest of the herbs and rice powder, and serve with sticky rice and crisp vegetables to scoop it up.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Crumble the tofu small so it holds the dressing like minced meat.
Season off the heat so the lime stays bright and fresh.
Toasted rice powder is essential: it adds a nutty crunch and soaks up the juices.
vegetarian.make_ahead: The toasted rice powder keeps 2 months in a sealed jar. Larb is best eaten right after mixing.

vegetarian.title: Vegetarian Mantu
vegetarian.description: The same steamed dumplings with a filling of mushrooms, lentils and onion, under garlic yogurt and tomato split pea sauce.

ingredients.item: all-purpose flour, plus more for rolling
finely chopped mushrooms and 1 cup cooked brown lentils

steps: Mix the flour, salt and water into a firm dough. Knead 5 minutes, cover and rest 30 minutes.
Cook the mushrooms and half the onion in a little oil until dry and browned, then mix with the lentils, coriander, pepper and salt for the filling.

Simmer the split peas in water for 30 minutes until tender, then drain. In the oil, soften the rest of the onion, add the garlic, tomato paste, tomato and paprika and a cup of water, then the split peas. Simmer 10 minutes into a thick sauce.
Roll the dough very thin and cut into 3 1/2-inch squares. Put a spoon of filling in each, bring two opposite corners together, then pinch the other two corners up to seal.
Steam the dumplings on oiled steamer racks for 25 to 30 minutes, until the wrappers are tender and translucent.
Stir the grated garlic and a pinch of salt into the yogurt. Spread half on a platter, arrange the mantu on top, spoon over the tomato sauce and remaining yogurt, and finish with dried mint.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Roll the dough as thin as you can; thick wrappers turn doughy when steamed.
Cook the mushrooms until all their water is gone, or the filling will make the wrappers soggy.
The cool yogurt, warm sauce and dried mint together are what make mantu, so don't skip any of them.
vegetarian.make_ahead: Freeze shaped, uncooked dumplings on a tray, then bag them; steam from frozen for 35 minutes. Both sauces keep 3 days.

vegetarian.title: Vegetarian Ropa Vieja
vegetarian.description: Young jackfruit and shredded oyster mushrooms simmered in the classic sofrito with peppers, olives and cumin.

ingredients.item: young green jackfruit in brine, drained and rinsed
green bell pepper, sliced into strips
red bell pepper, sliced into strips
white rice, black beans and fried sweet plantains, to serve

steps: Pull the jackfruit pieces into shreds with your fingers, discarding any hard seeds.
Brown the mushrooms in 1 tbsp oil over high heat for 5 minutes. Add the remaining oil, onion and peppers and cook 8 minutes until soft. Add the garlic, cumin and oregano for 1 minute.
Add the wine for 2 minutes, then the tomato sauce, broth, bay leaf, jackfruit, olives, capers and salt.
Simmer, uncovered, for 20 to 25 minutes, mashing the jackfruit a little, until thick and saucy. Serve with rice, black beans and plantains.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Young green jackfruit in brine (not syrup) shreds into strands just like the beef.
vegetarian.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen.

vegetarian.title: Vegetarian Caldo Verde
vegetarian.description: The same silky potato and greens soup with smoked paprika oil and white beans in place of the chouriço.

ingredients.item: extra-virgin olive oil, plus more to serve
floury potatoes (Yukon Gold or russet), peeled and cut in chunks
collard greens or lacinato kale, stems removed
black pepper and crusty cornbread (broa), to serve

steps: Cook the onion in the olive oil for 6 to 8 minutes, until soft, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the potatoes, water and salt. Bring to a boil and simmer, partly covered, for 20 minutes, until the potatoes fall apart.
Meanwhile, slice the greens into very fine ribbons. In a small pan, warm 3 tbsp olive oil with the smoked paprika for 1 minute and toss the beans in it.

vegetarian.description: Silky okra cou-cou topped with seasoned eggplant steamed in the same tomato and pepper creole sauce.

ingredients.item: small eggplants, sliced into thick rounds

vegetarian.description: King oyster mushroom planks pressed flat, seasoned the Bahamian way and fried crisp in the same egg and flour coating.

steps: Toss the mushroom planks with the lime juice and a pinch of salt.

Whisk the eggs and milk in one dish. In another, mix the flour, garlic powder, seasoned salt, cayenne, pepper and thyme.
Heat 2 inches of oil to 350°F. Dip the mushrooms in flour, then egg, then flour again, pressing the coating on.
Fry 2 or 3 pieces at a time for 2 to 3 minutes, turning once, until golden and crisp. The mushrooms should be tender inside.

vegetarian.title: Vegetarian Dan Dan Noodles
vegetarian.description: Crisp, savory chopped mushrooms and tofu in place of pork, over noodles in the same numbing sesame and chili sauce.

ingredients.item: mixed mushrooms and firm tofu, finely chopped
sui mi ya cai (Sichuan preserved mustard greens)
hot noodle water or vegetable broth
roasted peanuts, crushed, and sliced green onions, to serve

steps: Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wok and stir-fry the mushrooms and tofu over medium-high heat for 8 to 10 minutes, until their liquid has cooked off and they are browned and crisp at the edges.
Add the Shaoxing wine, sweet bean sauce and dark soy sauce and cook 1 minute. Push the mushrooms aside, add the ya cai and stir for 30 seconds, then mix it in.
Whisk the sesame paste, light soy sauce, chili oil, vinegar, sugar, Sichuan pepper and garlic in a bowl, then loosen with the hot noodle water or broth.
Cook the noodles according to the package. Add the bok choy for the last minute, then drain.
Divide the sauce among four bowls, add the noodles and greens and top with the mushroom crumble, peanuts and green onions. Toss everything together at the table.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

vegetarian.title: Vegetable Momos
vegetarian.description: Steamed dumplings filled with cabbage, carrot, tofu and ginger, with the same smoky tomato and sesame achar.

ingredients.item: finely chopped cabbage, salted 10 minutes and squeezed dry, plus 1 grated carrot and 7 oz crumbled firm tofu

steps: Mix the flour and water into a smooth, firm dough. Knead 5 minutes, cover and rest 30 minutes.
Mix the cabbage, carrot, tofu, red onion, green onions, ginger, garlic, cilantro, cumin, coriander, turmeric, 1 tsp salt and oil. Chill while you make the achar.

Char the tomatoes and chilies in a dry pan or under the broiler until blackened in spots. Blend them with the toasted sesame, lime juice, timur, the rest of the salt and a little water into a thick sauce.
Roll the dough into a log, cut into 30 pieces and roll each into a thin 3 1/2-inch circle, thinner at the edges.
Put a spoon of filling in the center and pleat the edges together into a round purse, twisting the top to seal.
Steam on oiled racks for 10 to 12 minutes, until the wrappers are glossy and tender (165°F). Serve hot with the achar.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Roll the wrapper edges thinner than the center, so the pleated top isn't doughy.
Squeeze the salted cabbage well, or the filling will turn watery and tear the wrappers.
Charring the tomatoes gives the achar its smoky depth; don't skip it.
vegetarian.make_ahead: Freeze shaped momos on a tray, then bag them; steam from frozen for 15 minutes. The achar keeps 5 days.

vegetarian.title: Vegetarian Nasi Lemak
vegetarian.description: Coconut pandan rice with a belacan-free sambal, crisp fried tempeh in place of anchovies, peanuts, egg and cucumber.

ingredients.item: pandan leaves, tied in a knot
dried red chilies, soaked and seeded
white miso or a little extra salt

steps: Put the rice, coconut milk, water, pandan, ginger and salt in a pot or rice cooker. Cook as you would plain rice, then rest 10 minutes and fluff.
Blend the chilies, shallots, garlic and miso into a paste with a splash of water.
Fry the tempeh in 1/4 cup oil until crisp and golden, about 5 minutes, then the peanuts for 2 to 3 minutes until golden. Drain both.

In the same oil, fry the chili paste over medium-low heat for 10 to 15 minutes, stirring, until dark red and the oil separates. Add the onion rings, tamarind water and sugar and simmer 5 minutes. Stir in a third of the tempeh.
Mound the rice on plates and serve with sambal, tempeh, peanuts, egg and cucumber around it.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Cook the sambal paste slowly until the oil splits away. Rushing it leaves a raw, harsh chili taste.
Fry the tempeh and peanuts separately; they cook at different speeds.
Serve on a banana leaf for the classic aroma.
vegetarian.make_ahead: The sambal keeps 2 weeks in the fridge and freezes well. Store the fried tempeh and peanuts airtight for 1 week.

vegetarian.description: The same fiery spiced broth with meaty mushrooms, plantain and yam simmered in it.

ingredients.item: oyster or king oyster mushrooms, torn into big pieces
green plantain, peeled and cut in chunks
yam or potato, peeled and cut in chunks
pepper soup spice (ehuru, uda, uziza blend)
uziza, utazi or scent leaves (or basil), chopped

steps: Brown the mushrooms in a little oil in a large pot for 5 minutes. Add the onion, half the peppers and the ginger for 2 minutes.
Add the water, stock cubes, salt, plantain and yam. Simmer, partly covered, for 25 minutes, until the yam is tender.

vegan.title: Vegan Pasta alla Norma
vegan.description: The same fried eggplant and tomato pasta, finished with toasted garlic breadcrumbs instead of ricotta salata.

salt, plus more for the pasta water
olive oil, for frying, plus 2 tbsp

steps: Toss the eggplant with 1 tsp salt and let it drain in a colander for 30 minutes. Pat very dry.
Fry the eggplant in the 1/2 cup oil in batches over medium-high heat for 6 to 8 minutes, until deep golden and creamy inside. Drain on paper towels.
In a clean pan, warm the 2 tbsp oil with the garlic and chili flakes until the garlic is pale gold. Add the tomatoes, 1/2 tsp salt and a few basil leaves. Simmer 15 minutes, until thickened.
Cook the pasta in well-salted water until al dente. Save a cup of the cooking water.

vegan.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Salting the eggplant draws out water, so it fries up creamy instead of soaking up oil.

vegetarian.title: Romanian Sour Mushroom Soup
vegetarian.description: The tripe soup's silky sour cream, egg yolk, vinegar and garlic finish, made with strips of oyster mushrooms in a root vegetable broth.

ingredients.item: celery root, peeled, or 2 celery stalks
garlic, crushed to a paste with a pinch of salt
white wine vinegar, plus more to taste
hot peppers and extra sour cream, to serve

steps: Simmer the broth with the carrots, parsnip, celery root, onion and bay leaves for 30 minutes. Lift out the vegetables and cut the carrot into matchsticks.
Brown the mushroom strips in the oil over high heat for 6 to 8 minutes. Add them and the carrot to the broth with the salt and simmer 10 minutes.

Whisk the sour cream and egg yolks in a bowl. Slowly whisk in 2 ladles of hot broth, then stir the mixture back into the pot over low heat. Heat gently until steaming (160°F) so the yolks cook through, but don't let it boil.
Stir in half the garlic paste and the vinegar. Taste and add more vinegar or salt until it's pleasantly sour. Serve with hot peppers, more garlic and sour cream on the side.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.

vegan.description: Oyster mushrooms in a root vegetable broth, thickened with cashew cream and finished with vinegar and garlic.

garlic, crushed to a paste with a pinch of salt

vegetarian.title: Vegetarian Plov
vegetarian.description: The same golden carrot and cumin rice with whole garlic, built on a zirvak of chickpeas and browned mushrooms instead of lamb.

ingredients.item: cremini or king oyster mushrooms, halved
large onions, sliced into half moons
yellow and orange carrots, cut into thick matchsticks
garlic, loose outer skin removed, left whole
medium-grain or basmati rice, rinsed until clear and soaked 30 minutes
sliced tomato and onion salad (achichuk), to serve

steps: Heat the oil in a heavy wide pot or Dutch oven until very hot. Brown the mushrooms in batches for 6 to 8 minutes, until deeply colored.
Add the onions and cook 5 to 8 minutes until golden, then the carrots. Cook 10 minutes without much stirring, until the carrots soften.
Make the zirvak: add half the cumin, the coriander, barberries, chili, 2 tsp salt, chickpeas and enough boiling water to just cover. Simmer, covered, for 20 minutes.
Drain the rice and spread it evenly over the zirvak. Don't stir. Pour boiling water gently over a spoon to come 1/2 inch above the rice. Add the remaining salt and cumin.
Boil, uncovered, until the water drops below the rice surface. Push the garlic heads into the rice, then gather the rice into a dome and poke 6 holes down to the bottom.
Cover tightly and cook on the lowest heat for 25 to 30 minutes, until the rice is tender. Rest 10 minutes.
Mix gently, mound on a platter with the mushrooms, chickpeas and carrots on top and the garlic heads in the center. Serve with a fresh tomato and onion salad.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Never stir once the rice goes on. The rice steams in layers above the zirvak and soaks up its flavor.
Cut the carrots by hand into thick matchsticks; grated carrots turn to mush.
Squeeze the soft, sweet garlic cloves onto your rice as you eat.
vegetarian.make_ahead: Keeps 4 days in the fridge. Reheat with a splash of water, covered, so it steams.

vegetarian.description: The same tangy sauerkraut and cabbage stew, made smoky with smoked paprika and rich with plenty of fresh and dried mushrooms.

ingredients.item: smoked tofu, cubed, and 2 tsp smoked paprika
salt and plenty of black pepper

steps: Soak the porcini in the boiling water for 20 minutes. Lift them out, chop them, and keep the soaking liquid, leaving any grit behind.
Heat the oil in a large heavy pot. Brown the fresh mushrooms for 6 to 8 minutes, then the smoked tofu for 3 minutes. Lift everything out.
Cook the onion in the same pot for 5 minutes. Add the cabbage and cook 10 minutes until it wilts.
Add the sauerkraut, browned mushrooms and tofu, the porcini and their liquid, prunes, wine, tomato paste and all the spices. Stir well.

vegetarian.title: Mushroom Paprikash
vegetarian.description: Meaty mushrooms simmered in the same onion, paprika and sour cream sauce, served over buttered nokedli.

ingredients.item: mixed mushrooms (cremini, oyster, king oyster), thickly sliced
Hungarian wax or bell pepper, chopped
full-fat sour cream, at room temperature

steps: Brown the mushrooms in the oil in a wide pot over high heat, in batches, for 6 to 8 minutes. Season with 1 tsp salt and lift out.
Cook the onions in the fat for 10 minutes until soft and golden. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the paprika, so it doesn't burn. Add the pepper, tomato, broth and the rest of the salt, then return the mushrooms.
Simmer gently, uncovered, for 10 minutes to blend the flavors.

Meanwhile, make the nokedli: mix the flour, eggs, water and a pinch of salt into a thick, sticky batter. Scrape small bits into simmering salted water with a spoon or spaetzle maker. When they float, cook 1 minute more, drain and toss with butter.
Whisk the sour cream and 1 tbsp flour, then whisk in a ladle of the hot sauce. Stir it into the pot and simmer gently 2 to 3 minutes until thickened. Serve over the nokedli.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Always add paprika off the heat. Scorched paprika turns bitter in seconds.
Real Hungarian sweet paprika makes the biggest difference; it's richer and redder than generic paprika.
Temper the sour cream with hot sauce first so it doesn't split.

vegetarian.title: Tofu and Chickpea Yassa
vegetarian.description: Grilled tofu and chickpeas simmered in the same lemony mustard sauce with sweet caramelized onions and olives.

ingredients.item: extra-firm tofu, pressed and cut into thick slabs, plus 1 can (15 oz) chickpeas, drained
Scotch bonnet chili, left whole and pricked
gluten-free vegetable stock cube (such as Herb-Ox)
white or broken rice, to serve

steps: Whisk the lemon juice, 2 tbsp mustard, garlic, vinegar, half the oil, salt and pepper. Toss the tofu and onions in it and marinate at least 1 hour, or overnight.
Lift the tofu out, shaking off the onions, and grill or broil it for 4 to 5 minutes a side, until well browned.
Lift the onions from the marinade (keep the liquid). Cook them in the remaining oil in a wide pot over medium heat for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring often, until soft and golden.
Add the marinade, remaining mustard, chili, bay leaf, vegetable stock cube and water. Nestle in the tofu and add the chickpeas.
Cover and simmer gently for 15 minutes so the tofu soaks up the sauce. Add the olives for the last 5 minutes. Serve over rice with plenty of onion sauce.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: The onions are the star. Give them time to soften and turn sweet before the tofu goes in.
Grilling the tofu first adds a smoky char and helps it hold together.
Keep the chili whole for flavor and gentle heat; break it open if you like it fiery.
vegetarian.make_ahead: Marinate up to a day ahead. The finished dish keeps 4 days and tastes even better reheated.

vegetarian.title: Creamy Dill Soup with Smoked Tofu
vegetarian.description: The same leek, potato and dill soup with allspice and cream, with smoked tofu in place of salmon.

ingredients.item: leek, white and light green parts, sliced
waxy potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks
salt and white pepper, to taste
rye bread and butter, to serve

steps: Melt the butter in a pot and soften the leek for 5 minutes without browning.
Add the potatoes, carrots, stock, bay leaf, allspice and salt. Simmer 15 minutes, until the potatoes are just tender.
Turn the heat to low. Add the cream, smoked tofu and most of the dill.
Cook very gently for 4 to 5 minutes, without boiling, until warmed through. Season with pepper and serve with the rest of the dill and rye bread.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Keep the soup below a boil once the cream goes in so it doesn't split.
Fresh dill is essential; dried dill doesn't come close.
Smoked tofu gives the gentle smoky depth that salmon brings.
vegetarian.make_ahead: Best eaten fresh. Leftovers keep 2 days; reheat gently without boiling.

vegan.title: Vegan Creamy Dill Soup with Smoked Tofu
vegan.description: Leek, potato and smoked tofu in a dill and allspice broth made creamy with oat cream.

ingredients.item: leek, white and light green parts, sliced
waxy potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks

vegetarian.title: Tofu Katsudon
vegetarian.description: A crisp panko tofu cutlet simmered with onions in kombu dashi, soy and mirin, softly set with egg over rice.

ingredients.item: slabs of extra-firm tofu (about 5 oz each), pressed, 3/4 inch thick
salt and a pinch of pepper

steps: Pat the tofu very dry. Season, then coat in flour, beaten egg and panko.
Fry in 1/2 inch of oil at 350°F for 2 to 3 minutes a side, until golden and crisp. Drain on a rack and slice into strips.
In a small frying pan, simmer the kombu kombu dashi or mushroom broth, soy sauce, mirin and sugar with the onion for 3 to 4 minutes, until the onion is soft.
Lay one sliced cutlet on the onions. Pour half the beaten eggs around and over it, cover and cook 1 minute, until the egg is just barely set.
Slide it over a bowl of rice and top with green onion. Repeat for the second bowl.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Beat the eggs only lightly so you can still see streaks of white and yolk. That marbled look is the classic finish.
Pour the egg around the cutlet, not all over it, so part of the crust stays crisp.
Press the tofu for 20 minutes so the coating stays crisp.
The egg is served softly set. For anyone pregnant, older or with a weakened immune system, cook it until firm or use pasteurized eggs.
vegetarian.make_ahead: Fry the tofu cutlets up to a day ahead and reheat in the oven. Cook the egg topping just before serving.

vegan.title: Vegan Tofu Katsudon
vegan.description: A crisp tofu cutlet in sweet-savory kombu dashi with onions, topped with a soft-set silken tofu "egg" over rice.

ingredients.item: slabs of extra-firm tofu (about 5 oz each), pressed, 3/4 inch thick
salt and a pinch of pepper
silken tofu, blended with 1 tbsp cornstarch, a pinch of turmeric and a pinch of salt

steps: Pat the firm tofu very dry and season it. Whisk 1/4 cup flour with the water into a smooth batter. Coat the tofu in plain flour, then batter, then panko.
Fry in 1/2 inch of oil at 350°F for 2 to 3 minutes a side, until golden and crisp. Drain and slice into strips.
In a small frying pan, simmer the kombu dashi, soy sauce, mirin and sugar with the onion for 3 to 4 minutes, until the onion is soft.
Lay one sliced cutlet on the onions. Spoon half the silken tofu mixture around it, cover and cook 2 to 3 minutes, until softly set.
Slide it over a bowl of rice and top with green onion. Repeat for the second bowl.
vegan.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: The silken tofu, cornstarch and turmeric mixture sets softly like egg in the hot sauce.
Press the firm tofu for 20 minutes so the coating stays crisp.
vegan.make_ahead: Fry the tofu cutlets up to a day ahead and reheat in the oven.

vegetarian.title: Mangú with Fried Cheese and Eggs
vegetarian.description: Buttery mashed green plantains with tangy red onions, fried cheese, fried eggs and avocado, without the salami.

ingredients.item: green (unripe) plantains, peeled and cut in chunks
cold water, from the plantain pot
large red onion, sliced into rings
portobello mushrooms, sliced thick and seasoned with smoked paprika
queso de freír (frying cheese), sliced 1/2 inch thick

steps: Boil the plantains in salted water for 15 to 20 minutes, until very tender.
Meanwhile, cook the onion rings in the olive oil for 3 minutes, add the vinegar and a pinch of salt and cook 2 minutes more, until just softened and tangy.
Drain the plantains, keeping some of the water. Mash them with the butter, adding cold water a little at a time, until smooth and creamy.
Fry the mushroom slices in a little oil for 3 minutes a side until browned. Fry the cheese in the same pan for 1 to 2 minutes a side until golden.
Fry the eggs sunny side up.
Pile the mangú on plates, top with the onions and their juices, and serve with the mushrooms, cheese, eggs and avocado.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Mash the plantains while they're hot and add the water cold. Dominican cooks swear it makes the mangú extra smooth.
Use fully green plantains; ripe ones make a sweet, different dish.
Pat the cheese dry before frying so it browns instead of spattering.
Sunny-side-up eggs have runny yolks. For anyone pregnant, older or with a weakened immune system, cook them until firm or use pasteurized eggs.
vegetarian.make_ahead: Mangú stiffens as it cools; reheat with a splash of water and stir until smooth.

vegetarian.title: Vegetarian Mohinga
vegetarian.description: The same golden lemongrass broth thickened with toasted rice and chickpea flour, made with oyster mushrooms and soy sauce instead of fish.

ingredients.item: lemongrass, bruised, plus 1 stalk finely chopped
rice flour, toasted in a dry pan until golden
chickpea flour, toasted in a dry pan until golden
small shallots, peeled and left whole
sliced banana stem or banana blossom (optional)
cilantro, lime wedges, chili flakes, fried onions and split pea fritters, to serve

steps: Simmer the water with the bruised lemongrass, sliced ginger, 1 tsp turmeric and 1 tbsp soy sauce for 15 minutes. Strain and keep the broth.
In a large pot, fry the onions in the oil for 8 minutes until golden. Add the garlic, grated ginger, chopped lemongrass, miso, paprika, chili flakes and the rest of the turmeric for 2 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and stir for 4 minutes. Pour in the broth.
Whisk the toasted rice flour and chickpea flour with a cup of water until smooth, then stir into the pot. Add the shallots and banana stem.
Simmer 30 minutes, stirring often, until thickened and the shallots are soft. Season with the remaining soy sauce.
Put noodles in each bowl, ladle the soup over and top with egg, cilantro, lime, chili and crunchy fritters or fried onions.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Toast the rice flour and chickpea flour until nutty and golden; this gives the broth its body and flavor.
Whisk the flours into cold water before adding them, so the soup stays smooth.
The crunchy toppings matter as much as the soup. Don't skip the fritters or fried onions.
vegetarian.make_ahead: The broth keeps 3 days in the fridge or 3 months frozen. Cook the noodles fresh.

vegetarian.description: A vegetarian take on samgyetang: ginseng, jujubes, garlic and sweet rice simmered with shiitake, king oyster mushrooms and tofu into a soothing broth.

fresh ginseng roots (or 2 tbsp dried ginseng)
salt and black pepper, at the table

steps: Simmer the water with the shiitake, kombu, ginseng, ginger, garlic and jujubes for 20 minutes. Remove the kombu.

Add the king oyster mushrooms and tofu and simmer 5 minutes more.
Serve in large bowls, scattered with green onion. Season with salt and pepper at the table and eat with kimchi.

vegan.description: Olive-oil-poached potatoes and onion folded into a chickpea flour batter and cooked into a golden, sliceable cake.

ingredients.item: Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced

steps: Heat the oil in a 10-inch nonstick skillet over medium-low heat. Add the potatoes, onion and 1 tsp salt. Cook gently for 20 to 25 minutes, turning now and then, until completely tender but not browned.

tips: Chickpea flour needs a little longer than egg to set, so cook it a few minutes more on each side.

vegan.title: Vegan Amaretto Sour
vegan.description: The same rich, bright amaretto sour, with aquafaba (chickpea water) whipped into the foam instead of egg white.

ingredients.item: aquafaba (liquid from a can of chickpeas)

steps: Shake the amaretto, bourbon, lemon juice, syrup and aquafaba without ice for 15 seconds to build the foam.
Add ice and shake hard for 10 seconds more.
Strain into a rocks glass over fresh ice. Garnish with an orange slice and cherry, and dot the foam with bitters.

vegan.title: Vegan Brooklynite
vegan.description: The same rum and lime classic, sweetened with agave syrup instead of honey.
steps: Shake the rum, lime juice, agave syrup and bitters with ice until very cold.

Garnish with a lime twist.

tips: Agave mixes in easily; add a little less if your agave is very sweet.

ingredients.item: oz aquafaba plus 1/2 oz oat milk

steps: Shake the tequila, Chartreuse, Jägermeister, syrup, aquafaba and oat milk without ice for 15 seconds.
Add ice and shake hard for 10 seconds more.
Fine strain into a small chilled coupe or wine glass and grate nutmeg over the top.

vegan.title: Vegan Hotel Georgia

Add ice and shake hard again.

tips: Double strain through a fine sieve to catch the raspberry seeds.

vegan.title: Vegan B-52
vegan.description: The same layered shot made with an almond-based vegan Irish cream.

steps: Pour the coffee liqueur into a shot glass.
Slowly pour the vegan Irish cream over the back of a bar spoon so it floats on top.
Float the Grand Marnier the same way to make the top layer.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Layer cold coffee syrup, a little oat cream and orange syrup in a shot glass.

vegan.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Pour very slowly over the back of a spoon held just above the last layer.
Chill the liqueurs first; cold layers stay separate more easily.

vegan.title: Vegan Three Dots and a Dash
vegan.description: The same rhum and allspice tiki drink, sweetened with agave syrup instead of honey.
steps: Put all the ingredients in a blender with the crushed ice.
Flash blend for 5 seconds.
Pour into a tulip or tiki glass. Garnish with three cherries and a pineapple spear on a pick: the three dots and the dash.

cocktail.garnish: three cherries and a pineapple spear
cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Flash blend lime, orange juice, honey syrup, a pinch of allspice and crushed ice.

vegan.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: Allspice dram is potent; measure it carefully.
The garnish spells "V" in Morse code: dot, dot, dot, dash.

vegetarian.title: Tom Kha Hed (Thai Coconut Mushroom Soup)
vegetarian.description: A creamy Thai soup of tofu and mushrooms simmered in coconut milk and vegetable broth with galangal, lemongrass and lime leaves, finished with lime and soy sauce.

ingredients.item: lemongrass, bottom halves only, smashed and cut into 2-inch pieces
oyster or straw mushrooms, torn into bite-size pieces
light soy sauce, plus more to taste
palm sugar or light brown sugar
fresh lime juice, plus more to taste

steps: Bring the broth to a simmer in a pot. Add the lemongrass, galangal, lime leaves and chilies and simmer for 5 minutes to release their flavor.
Add the coconut milk and tofu and bring back to a gentle simmer. Cook for 3 minutes.
Add the mushrooms, soy sauce and sugar and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes more, until the mushrooms are tender.
Turn off the heat and stir in the lime juice.
Taste: it should be sour and salty first, then creamy. Add more lime or soy sauce if needed. Serve topped with cilantro.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Keep it at a gentle simmer once the coconut milk is in. A hard boil can make it split.
The lemongrass, galangal and lime leaves are for flavor, not for eating. Leave them in the pot when you serve.
Galangal is not the same as ginger, but ginger will do in a pinch.
vegetarian.make_ahead: Refrigerate for up to 2 days. Reheat gently and add a fresh squeeze of lime.

vegetarian.title: Vegetable Tempura
vegetarian.description: Sweet potato, eggplant, shiitake and zucchini in a light, ice-cold batter, fried crisp and served with a kombu and soy dipping sauce.

ingredients.item: small sweet potato, cut into 1/4-inch rounds
small Japanese eggplant, cut into 1/4-inch slices
all-purpose flour, plus 1/4 cup for dusting
ice-cold water, plus a few ice cubes
vegetable or canola oil, for frying
kombu broth (a 4-inch piece of kombu soaked in 1 cup water for 30 minutes)
finely grated daikon radish, to serve
finely grated fresh ginger, to serve

steps: Make the dipping sauce: bring the kombu broth, soy sauce and mirin to a simmer in a small pan, then turn off the heat and let it cool.
Pat the vegetables very dry.
Heat 2 inches of oil in a heavy pot to 340°F.
Make the batter right before frying: whisk the egg and ice water in a bowl, add 1 cup flour all at once and stir just a few strokes with chopsticks. Lumps are fine.
Dust each piece lightly in the extra flour, dip it in the batter and let the excess drip off.
Fry a few pieces at a time for 2 to 3 minutes, turning once, until crisp and pale gold. Drain on a rack.
Serve right away with the dipping sauce, grated daikon and ginger.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Keep the batter ice-cold and barely mixed. Stirring builds gluten, which makes the coating heavy and bready.
The dusting of flour helps the batter cling, especially to smooth vegetables.
Skim floating bits of batter from the oil between batches so they don't burn.

vegan.title: Vegan Vegetable Tempura
vegan.description: Sweet potato, eggplant, shiitake and zucchini in an egg-free batter made with ice-cold sparkling water, fried crisp and served with a kombu and soy dipping sauce.

ingredients.item: small sweet potato, cut into 1/4-inch rounds
small Japanese eggplant, cut into 1/4-inch slices
all-purpose flour, plus 1/4 cup for dusting

vegetable or canola oil, for frying
kombu broth (a 4-inch piece of kombu soaked in 1 cup water for 30 minutes)

vegetarian.title: Avocado and Cucumber Maki Rolls
vegetarian.description: Classic thin sushi rolls of seasoned rice and nori, half filled with creamy avocado and half with crisp cucumber. Served with soy sauce, wasabi and pickled ginger.

ingredients.item: ripe avocado, cut into thin strips
Japanese or Persian cucumber, cut into thin sticks

steps: Rinse the rice in a bowl of cold water, swirling and draining, 4 or 5 times until the water runs almost clear. Drain for 15 minutes.
Cook the rice with the water in a rice cooker, or in a covered pot: boil, then simmer on low for 15 minutes and rest off the heat, still covered, for 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, warm the vinegar, sugar and salt in a small pan, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Let it cool.

Spread the hot rice in a wide bowl. Drizzle the vinegar mixture over it and fold with a spatula, cutting through the rice rather than stirring, while fanning it to cool. Cover with a damp towel until it's at room temperature.

Lay a bamboo mat on the counter and place a half sheet of nori on it, shiny side down. Wet your hands and spread a thin, even layer of rice over the nori, leaving a 1/2-inch strip bare at the far edge.
Lay a line of avocado across the middle of the rice for 3 of the rolls, and cucumber for the other 3.
Lift the near edge of the mat and roll it over the filling, pressing gently, then keep rolling until the bare strip of nori seals the roll.
Cut each roll into 6 pieces with a sharp, wet knife, wiping the blade between cuts. Serve with wasabi, pickled ginger and soy sauce.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Keep a bowl of water with a splash of vinegar beside you. Wet hands stop the rice from sticking to your fingers.
Use less rice than you think. A thin layer keeps the roll neat and lets the filling stand out.
Cool the rice to room temperature before rolling: hot rice makes the nori go limp.
vegetarian.make_ahead: Sushi is best eaten within a few hours. Don't refrigerate it, because cold makes the rice hard.

vegetarian.title: Vegetarian Miso Soup
vegetarian.description: Japan's everyday miso soup made with a kombu and shiitake broth, plus soft tofu, wakame seaweed and scallions.

ingredients.item: miso paste (white or red), plus more to taste
silken or soft tofu, cut into 1/2-inch cubes

steps: Soak the kombu and dried shiitake in the water in a saucepan for 30 minutes.
Heat the pan slowly over medium-low heat and simmer gently for 5 minutes. Lift out the kombu and mushrooms; slice the mushrooms and return them to the broth.
Soak the wakame in a bowl of water for 5 minutes, then drain.
Warm the broth over low heat. Put the miso in a ladle or small sieve, lower it into the broth and whisk until it dissolves.
Add the tofu and wakame and heat gently for 1 to 2 minutes. Do not let the soup boil.
Ladle into bowls and top with the scallions.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Never boil miso soup once the miso is in. Boiling dulls its aroma and flavor.
Start with 1 tablespoon of miso per cup of broth and add more to taste. Brands vary in saltiness.
vegetarian.make_ahead: Make the kombu and shiitake broth up to 3 days ahead and keep it in the fridge. Add the miso and tofu just before serving.

vegetarian.title: Vegetarian Som Tam
vegetarian.description: Thailand's crunchy, fiery green papaya salad, seasoned with soy sauce and lime instead of fish sauce and dried shrimp.

ingredients.item: Thai bird's eye chilies, to taste
yard-long beans or 6 green beans, cut into 2-inch pieces

steps: In a large mortar, pound the garlic and chilies to a rough paste.
Add the palm sugar and pound until it softens.
Add the long beans and peanuts and pound a few times, just to bruise the beans and break the peanuts.
Add the soy sauce, lime juice and tamarind paste, if using, and stir until the sugar dissolves.
Add the papaya and tomatoes. Pound lightly while turning everything with a spoon, for about 1 minute, until the papaya softens slightly and soaks up the dressing.
Taste: it should be sour, salty, sweet and spicy. Adjust with more lime, soy sauce or sugar and serve right away.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: No mortar? Mash the garlic, chilies and sugar in a large bowl with the end of a rolling pin, then toss everything together.
Use a julienne peeler for the papaya. Shreds that are too thick won't soak up the dressing.
For a gluten-free version, use tamari instead of soy sauce.

vegan.title: Vegan Tofu Fried Rice
vegan.description: The everyday Chinese fried rice made with crumbled tofu instead of scrambled egg, plus peas, carrot and scallions, all tossed in a very hot pan.

ingredients.item: cold cooked jasmine rice, ideally a day old
firm tofu, patted dry and crumbled
scallions, thinly sliced, whites and greens kept apart

steps: Break up any clumps of rice with your fingers so the grains are separate.

Heat a wok or large skillet over high heat until it just starts to smoke. Add 1 tablespoon of the oil and the tofu, sprinkle with the turmeric and a pinch of salt, and stir-fry for 3 minutes, until golden. Slide it onto a plate.
Add the rest of the oil, then the garlic and scallion whites. Stir for 15 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the peas and carrots and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the rice and spread it out. Let it sit for 30 seconds to toast, then toss. Repeat for 3 to 4 minutes, until every grain is hot and slightly chewy.
Add the soy sauce around the edge of the pan so it sizzles, then the sesame oil and white pepper. Toss well.
Return the tofu, add the scallion greens and toss once more. Taste for salt and serve right away.
vegan.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Cold, day-old rice is drier, so it fries into separate grains. Fresh rice steams and turns mushy.
The pinch of turmeric gives the tofu a golden color, and drying it well helps it brown.
Cook in two batches if your pan is small. A crowded pan can't stay hot enough to fry.
vegan.make_ahead: Keep leftovers in the fridge for up to 3 days and reheat in a hot pan with a splash of water.

vegan.title: Vegan Illegal
vegan.description: The same smoky mezcal sour, with aquafaba in place of the egg white.
steps: Chill a coupe or cocktail glass.
Add everything to a shaker and fill it with ice.
Shake hard for 15 seconds.
Strain into the chilled glass, or over fresh ice in a clay cup.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake 1 oz lime juice, 1/2 oz falernum syrup and 1 oz pineapple juice with ice, strain, and add 2 drops of liquid smoke if you like.

vegan.note: A classic home version. Bars vary the proportions, and this isn't any one bar's recipe. Please drink responsibly.
tips: The small splash of aquafaba is only for texture. Leave it out and the drink is just as good.
Overproof rum is very strong. Measure it carefully.
Aquafaba foams like egg white and is safe to use raw.

vegetarian.title: Vegetarian Elote
vegetarian.description: Mexican street corn, charred and slathered in mayonnaise and crema, rolled in a salty cotija-style cheese made without animal rennet, with chile and lime.

ingredients.item: finely crumbled vegetarian cotija-style cheese (made with microbial rennet)
ancho or guajillo chile powder, plus more to serve

steps: Heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high. Brush the corn with oil and grill for 10 to 12 minutes, turning every couple of minutes, until tender and charred in spots.
Mix the mayonnaise and crema in a small bowl. Spread the cheese on a plate.
Brush each hot ear all over with the mayonnaise mixture, then roll it in the cheese, pressing so it sticks.
Sprinkle with chile powder and cilantro and serve with lime wedges for squeezing.
vegetarian.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Traditional cotija is made with animal rennet. Look for one labeled vegetarian or made with microbial rennet, or use a vegetarian feta.

vegan.description: Mexican street corn, charred and slathered in a creamy lime-chile sauce, rolled in crumbled vegan feta.

ingredients.item: ancho or guajillo chile powder, plus more to serve

steps: Heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high. Brush the corn with oil and grill for 10 to 12 minutes, turning every couple of minutes, until tender and charred in spots.
Stir the vegan mayo and dairy-free sour cream together in a small bowl. Spread the crumbled vegan feta on a plate.
Brush each hot ear all over with the sauce, then roll it in the crumbles, pressing so they stick.
Sprinkle with chile powder and cilantro and serve with lime wedges for squeezing.
vegan.note: A representative home version. Restaurants and regions make it in many ways, and this isn't any one restaurant's recipe.
tips: Check labels: some vegan mayonnaise contains soy, and some vegan cheeses are made from cashews or almonds.

vegan.title: Yuzu Agave Gin Sour
vegan.description: A yuzu gin sour sweetened with agave instead of honey.
steps: Combine gin, yuzu juice and agave syrup in a shaker.
Shake with ice for 15 seconds, then double-strain into a chilled coupe.
Express the lemon twist over the drink and add it.

cocktail.non_alcoholic_version: Shake 2 oz cooled green tea, 3/4 oz yuzu juice and 1/2 oz agave syrup with ice; strain into a coupe.

vegan.note: An original Relish home cocktail. Please drink responsibly.
tips: For agave syrup, stir equal volumes agave nectar and warm water until combined, then cool. Use food-grade yuzu juice rather than a sweetened concentrate.
vegan.make_ahead: Prepare to order. Keep juices and brewed teas refrigerated until needed.
